title: UPDATE: Barclays to Cut 5,000 Roles Including Support and Software Developers
summary:
Support functions and software developers will account for about 60% of the job losses announced by Barclays on Thursday. The bank plans to eliminate around 5,000 roles, or roughly 5% of its 93,000 staff, by the end of 2026, citing productivity gains from artificial intelligence. About 1,000 of those positions were already removed in the first half of 2026, with the remainder to be cut by year end.

The reductions come as Barclays posted a 12% increase in third-quarter pre-tax profit to £2.3B and announced a £500M share buyback. Chief Executive C.S. Venkatakrishnan described AI as the "icing rather than the cake," noting that savings depend on prior infrastructure. Similar AI-related cuts have been reported at American Express, Netflix, and eBay, while rivals HSBC and Standard Chartered are also weighing role reductions in corporate functions.

All these while 3rd-quarter pretax profit rose 12% to £2.3B. 
Among rivals, HSBC is reportedly weighing up to 20,000 role cuts over the coming years, while Standard Chartered plans to shrink corporate function roles by more than 15% by 2030.

Venkatakrishnan calls AI the icing rather than the cake, because its savings depend on infrastructure built beforehand.
